instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Confess First
cards.instruction: Get someone else to confess or incriminate themselves before you reveal anything.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before I explain the toaster in the bin, remember the incident reports I taught you to write. What happened to the printer?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It jammed. Now, the toaster?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Nearly. A report needs the person who did something. Who fed those sticky labels into it?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I did. They were the only labels left. Your turn.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good, a subject and a verb. Add 'although the packet said not for printers,' and then I'll start my report.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I taught you to own a mistake. Before I explain Mum's missing present, why was she outside the restaurant on her birthday?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I forgot the booking. What happened to the present?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Almost honest. Did you forget, or assume I'd do it for you?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I assumed you'd do it. I told her it was booked. Now you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good, you've got the facts in order. Say 'I promised without checking,' and I'll show you how to start a difficult explanation.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Sell the Disaster
cards.instruction: Make a terrible plan sound sensible, responsible, and inevitable.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Remember what I taught you about cutting overheads? Taking the restaurant roof off solves the ventilation bill permanently.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: And when rain gets on the tables?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good, you're thinking ahead. We close during rain; I didn't train you to serve wet dinners.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Rain is forecast all opening week. That's a week with no customers.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're finally forecasting properly. No customers means no food bill. Put that saving toward umbrellas; we can't afford to go back to paying for ventilation.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I taught you to honor a pledge. I've borrowed five thousand and sent the charity our expected auction takings. Now we must sell the lots.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Only your mum registered.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Well spotted. You're finally watching costs: one guest means almost no catering.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She's coming to drive us home. She isn't bidding.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we bid. This is the commitment lesson you keep missing. Ask for a higher card limit; that charity shouldn't suffer because we've run out of other people.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Fake the Expertise
cards.instruction: Perform expertise so confidently that no one questions you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I taught you to read a control panel. Watch closely and I'll get your boiler going.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That's the kitchen timer you're turning.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Excellent, you can identify the controls now. I'm establishing the heating interval. Ring the engineer while I supervise.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: He's asking what temperature you measured.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Don't rush to the numbers; I taught you to establish a baseline first. Put him on speaker and listen to how I ask the questions.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let me tune your violin for the audition. I taught you to hear a wrong note; I'll show you what to do about one.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You tightened that string until it snapped.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good ear. You've finally heard a string fail before an audience did. That was a stress test.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The panel heard it. They're asking whether you know what you're doing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Tell them your teacher rejected an unreliable string. Enunciate, like we practised. Then ask for their spare violin so I can approve it.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Everything Is a Contest
cards.instruction: Turn every difference or disagreement into a competition you intend to win.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I taught you to peel potatoes, and I'm still faster. First to finish five chooses dinner; I'm on four.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I want pizza. We can get it free with this voucher.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good, you've learned to compare prices. My potatoes are already here: free as well. Now compare preparation times.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The pizza arrives in ten minutes. Yours aren't even boiling.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then taste decides. I'll cook mine the way I taught you; Mum can judge. She's been asking me to make them all week.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I taught you to make tea, and yours is still half milk. Mine wins on strength.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Same pot. I wanted mine cool enough to drink.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good, you're thinking about efficiency. First empty cup wins, then; I've only two mouthfuls left.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Mine's empty. I'm making another.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Still haven't learned patience. Fewest refills wins. Watch your teacher make two mouthfuls last all breakfast.

cards.title: Brighter Side
cards.instruction: Meet every setback with even greater optimism.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: No tickets sold! Perfect: I can finish teaching you to project before anyone hears our play.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The theatre has cancelled us. They want the stage cleared.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Even better. You're ready to win over people who haven't come to listen. We'll hire the pub upstairs.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They kept our deposit. All we can afford is the bus home.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Wonderful, your first touring show! Start quietly at the back, like I taught you; by the next stop you'll have reached the whole bus.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The car won't start. Wonderful, a walking lesson! I taught you to navigate without that phone; now you can show me.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's pouring. I was hoping to stay dry.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Even better: you'll finally use my lesson about finding shelter. Lead us from awning to awning.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The next awning's gone, and my shoe's filling with water.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Wonderful, you've spotted when to ask for help! Try that cafe. I taught you to make friends; today you can get us indoors and make two.
